_comment: Every {placeholder} a template may name, read by BOTH languages — the same
referee as campaign-optional.json and campaign-env.json, for the same
reason: two implementations of one rule are one rule that drifts.
The engine is TypeScript and refuses an unknown placeholder at RENDER
time. Once a campaign writes its own templates, render time is the mass
mailing on a Sunday evening, or a volunteer's card that shows an error
instead of a message — so the API has to refuse the same text at SAVE
time, when the person who wrote it is looking at it. api/templates.go is
that second reader, and this file is what keeps it saying the same thing
as fields().
SPLIT BY RANK, because the split is the project's cardinal invariant. The
endorsement placeholders exist ONLY for someone who endorsed, and the
discovery ones ONLY for someone who did not: pasting "En {annee_recente},
vous avez présenté {candidat_recent}." into a discovery template printed
"En , vous avez présenté ." to 32 866 mayors, in silence. A template file
named *_decouverte.txt is judged against `common` + `discovery`, any other
against `common` + `has_endorsed`, and the two sets being DISJOINT is what
refuses that paste by name in either direction.
The direction of a stale copy: a name missing here refuses a template that
would in fact render — loudly, at save, to somebody who can report it. A
name here that fields() does not produce accepts a template the engine
will refuse at render, which is the failure this file exists to prevent.
TestThePlaceholderManifestMatchesTheEngine walks the second direction and
the first, so a field added to fields() goes red here before it can.
